---
title: "Inspect local remote versions"
---

Current source work: ordinary local latest/archive inspection. This command does
not upload, restore, verify artifact bytes or change configured remote definitions.
It is separate from CAS and the deferred registry design.

```bash
proj --project . remote versions --path /physical/path/to/archive --label raw-data
proj --machine --project . remote versions --path /physical/path/to/latest --label raw-data --structure latest
```

Paths relative to the command's selected project root are supported. Use physical
paths: symlinked parents, candidate directories and VERSION files are rejected.
No active project config, Git credentials or remote account are required.

Archive is the default layout: base/label/version directories. Numeric versions
sort newest first, including empty variants. The actual directory path is retained
even when version spellings differ. Multiple spellings or full/empty variants
remain visible rather than silently selecting one for restore. Unrelated names
are skipped; malformed numeric-looking version names and special candidates fail.

Latest reads the exact label entry from base/VERSION. It reports the trailing
asterisk as metadata_untrusted, plus present and empty fields. A missing target is
reported explicitly; an absent asterisk is **not proof of verified content**.
Archive results do not infer trust from metadata and return null for that field.
An absent base or VERSION yields no entries and creates nothing. Duplicate label
entries and malformed advertised versions are errors.

Use --path-append-label false only when version directories or latest contents
are directly at the supplied base. VERSION remains at that explicit base.
This makes the inspected path explicit; it is not a new remote registry format.

Machine output retains protocol v1 and adds a versions query result. No byte
verification, latest-source selection, credential discovery or publication occurs.
